papers.title: RRSI: Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses
papers.abstract: Abstract  An LLM agent's capability is largely magnified by its harness, namely the prompts, control flow, tooling, memory, and context management surrounding the frozen backbone model. Recent methods increasingly automate this process by iteratively proposing and selecting component-wise edits of an agent harness, practically establishing a form of recursive self-improvement (RSI) at the agent-system level. However, such recursive evolution may overfit by memorizing the training tasks, showing large in-distribution gains that shrink or even vanish on out-of-distribution benchmarks. We introduce Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement of Agent Harnesses (RRSI), which incorporates the principles of regularizations into harness self-improvement by constraining the evolution candidate proposal and selection. The proposer operates with a temporally annealed budget, limiting how many edits a candidate can bundle, and it encourages unexplored trajectories based on evolution history. The selector is equipped with a critic and a pruner: the critic screens benchmark-specific proposals, while the pruner, removes changes that are too small, too expensive, or no longer useful. Together these constraints favor reusable agent mechanisms over benchmark-specific ones or even noises. Across eight benchmarks spanning coding, agentic workspace and engineering design tasks, RRSI gains up to 14.1 points on the split it evolves against and up to 4.7 points on the five out-of-distribution benchmarks, while producing a harness that runs on 30% fewer policy tokens than the unregularized evolution. Code is available at https://github.com/google-research/rrsi and project page is https://regularized-rsi.com/.

ru.title: Регуляризированное самоулучшение агентских систем для лучшей обобщаемости
ru.desc: В работе предлагается метод RRSI для автоматической оптимизации архитектуры агентов на базе LLM путём итеративного улучшения их компонентов: промптов, управления потоком, инструментов и управления памятью. Основная проблема заключается в том, что неконтролируемое эволюционное улучшение приводит к переобучению на тренировочных задачах и плохой генерализации на новые примеры. Авторы вводят регуляризацию в процесс эволюции: ограничивают количество изменений в каждом кандидате, поощряют исследование новых траекторий и используют критика для отсеивания неполезных изменений. Результаты показывают значительное улучшение как на исходных бенчмарках, так и на внешних тестах, при этом финальный агент требует на 30% меньше токенов для работы.

en.title: Enhancing LLM Agents with Regularized Self-Improvement
en.desc: This paper discusses how to improve the performance of large language model (LLM) agents by refining their harness, which includes prompts and memory management. The authors introduce a method called Regularized Recursive Self-Improvement (RRSI) that applies regularization techniques to prevent overfitting during the agent's self-improvement process. RRSI uses a budget for edits and encourages exploration of new strategies while filtering out ineffective changes. The results show significant performance gains on both in-distribution and out-of-distribution tasks, while also reducing the number of policy tokens needed for operation.

zh.title: 优化代理工具的正则化自我改进
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种名为正则化递归自我改进（RRSI）的方法，用于优化大型语言模型（LLM）代理的工具和控制流程。RRSI通过引入正则化原则，限制代理自我改进过程中的候选提案和选择，从而避免过拟合训练任务。该方法使用时间退火预算来限制候选编辑的数量，并鼓励探索未开发的路径。实验结果表明，RRSI在多个基准测试中显著提高了性能，同时减少了所需的策略令牌数量。

papers.title: WorldCrafter: Consistent Video World Model with Implicit 3D-aware Memory
papers.abstract: Abstract  Video world models enable interactive exploration of dynamic environments, yet struggle to respect prior observations over long horizons and across viewpoints. We present WorldCrafter, a video world model that learns a camera-queryable implicit 3D-aware memory for this purpose. The key insight is to let the requested viewpoint shape how multi-view evidence is compressed into the video generator's limited token budget. Trained jointly with the video generator, a memory encoder and pose-conditioned readout module integrate historical observations into a fixed set of target view-specific tokens before denoising, without explicit depth-based correspondences. By combining this memory with recent temporal context and few-step distillation, WorldCrafter enables streaming scene exploration from a single input image or text prompt. Experiments across static and dynamic scenes show substantial gains in long-horizon consistency and camera-control accuracy while preserving visual quality during minute-scale exploration.

ru.title: Память сцены для контролируемого просмотра видео-миров
ru.desc: WorldCrafter — это видео-модель мира, которая строит трёхмерно-осознающую память сцены, запрашиваемую по камере, для воспроизведения динамических окружений. Ключевая идея заключается в том, чтобы запрошенная точка обзора определяла, как доказательства из нескольких видов сжимаются в ограниченный токен-бюджет видео-генератора. Модель обучается совместно с модулем кодирования памяти и модулем чтения, обусловленным позой камеры, которые интегрируют исторические наблюдения в фиксированный набор токенов перед процессом удаления шума. Комбинируя эту память с недавним временным контекстом и дистилляцией в несколько шагов, WorldCrafter позволяет исследовать сцену в режиме потока с одного входного изображения или текстового описания.

en.title: Enhancing Scene Exploration with WorldCrafter's 3D Memory
en.desc: WorldCrafter is a novel video world model designed to enhance the exploration of dynamic environments by effectively utilizing prior observations. It introduces a camera-queryable implicit 3D-aware memory that adapts to different viewpoints, allowing for better integration of multi-view evidence. The model employs a memory encoder and a pose-conditioned readout module to create view-specific tokens, which helps maintain consistency over long time horizons. Through experiments, WorldCrafter demonstrates improved accuracy in camera control and visual quality during extended scene exploration, even from minimal input data.

zh.title: WorldCrafter：动态环境中的智能视频探索
zh.desc: 视频世界模型可以让我们在动态环境中进行互动探索，但在长时间和不同视角下保持先前观察的准确性方面存在困难。我们提出了WorldCrafter，这是一种视频世界模型，能够学习一个可查询的隐式3D记忆，以解决这个问题。关键在于让请求的视角影响多视角证据如何压缩到视频生成器的有限令牌预算中。通过结合历史观察和最近的时间上下文，WorldCrafter能够从单个输入图像或文本提示中实现流式场景探索，同时在长时间一致性和相机控制精度上取得显著提升。

papers.title: GameHorizon Suite: Multi-Horizon Data and Evaluation in Gameplay
papers.abstract: Abstract  Modern video games provide a measurable testbed for AI models, combining abilities of visual understanding, instruction decomposition, goal planning, and precise action control over multiple temporal horizons. Existing datasets and benchmarks, however, either cover a narrow range of games, lack language instructions, or rely on high-variance online rollouts. To address these challenges, we introduce GameHorizon, a unified data and evaluation suite that measures gameplay capabilities at different horizons for diverse model families. GameHorizon Suite consists of three components. First, GameHorizon-Annotator is a scalable and automated annotation pipeline for multi-horizon instructions. Second, utilizing the pipeline, we construct GameHorizon-Data, the first large-scale AAA gameplay dataset with temporally aligned videos, player actions, and multi-horizon instructions. It comprises 5,000 hours of recordings from 21 games, collected by 100 human expert players. Third, we build GameHorizon-Bench with reproducible offline and stepwise online testing. The offline track enables reproducible evaluation using thousands of standardized questions organized into three primary tasks and a series of diagnostic variants, while the online track tests whether offline scores reflect actual gameplay capabilities and localizes failures to specific steps within long-horizon gameplay. Based on our GameHorizon Suite, we evaluate 47 models through more than one million model invocations, revealing a meaningful hierarchy of task difficulty and pronounced differences in model capabilities. Our work can provide a standardized yardstick for evaluating gameplay capabilities across horizons and model families. We will release our dataset, annotator, and benchmark to facilitate future research.
affiliations: Huazhong University of Science and Technology

ru.title: Универсальный бенчмарк для оценки игровых навыков AI на разных временных горизонтах
ru.desc: Исследователи представили GameHorizon — комплексный набор данных и инструментов оценки для тестирования способностей AI моделей в видеоиграх. Система включает автоматизированный конвейер аннотации для многоуровневых инструкций, большой датасет из 5000 часов геймплея от 21 AAA-игры с разметкой действий и целей на разных временных горизонтах, а также бенчмарк с воспроизводимым офлайн и онлайн тестированием. Авторы провели оценку 47 моделей через более миллиона вызовов, выявив иерархию сложности задач и различия в способностях моделей решать задачи визуального понимания, декомпозиции инструкций, планирования и управления действиями.

en.title: GameHorizon: A New Standard for Evaluating AI in Video Games
en.desc: This paper presents GameHorizon, a comprehensive suite designed to evaluate AI models in video games. It addresses limitations in existing datasets by providing a large-scale dataset with temporally aligned videos, player actions, and multi-horizon instructions from expert players. The suite includes an automated annotation pipeline and a benchmark for both offline and online testing, allowing for reproducible evaluations of model performance. The findings reveal a hierarchy of task difficulty and significant variations in model capabilities, establishing a standardized method for assessing gameplay skills across different AI models.

zh.title: GameHorizon：多时间范围游戏能力的标准化评估
zh.desc: 现代视频游戏为人工智能模型提供了一个可测量的测试平台，结合了视觉理解、指令分解、目标规划和多时间范围的精确动作控制。现有的数据集和基准测试要么覆盖的游戏范围狭窄，要么缺乏语言指令，或者依赖于高变异的在线回放。为了解决这些问题，我们推出了GameHorizon，一个统一的数据和评估套件，能够在不同的时间范围内测量多种模型的游戏能力。GameHorizon套件包括三个部分：自动注释管道、一个大型AAA游戏数据集和可重复的离线及在线测试基准。

papers.title: Transferring the Intelligence of VLMs to Robotic Control
papers.abstract: Abstract  Humans can seamlessly adapt to both physical and digital worlds, suggesting that while a digital-to-real gap exists in embodiment, environment and task, human intelligence itself may transfer across this gap. This naturally raises a fundamental question: can the intelligence of vision-language models (VLMs) similarly generalize from the digital world to the physical world for robotic control? We investigate this question through RoboDawn, a human-intuitive interface that exposes robotic control to an agentic VLM through a compact set of discrete translation, rotation, and gripper commands. Using this interface, the VLM controls a robot in a closed loop: it observes the current visual state, reasons about the next action, executes it, and adapts subsequent decisions to the resulting state. Furthermore, we introduce an in-context learning (ICL) scheme that uses a few demonstrations to ground the VLM in both interface usage and task-solving strategies. Experiments on RoboTwin 2.0 C2R and RoboDojo demonstrate that RoboDawn achieves strong performance without task-specific robot training. In the zero-shot setting, RoboDawn outperforms several strong policies trained on benchmarkspecific robot data, while a single in-context demonstration further yields substantial performance gains and establishes state-of-the-art (SOTA) results. On RoboTwin 2.0 C2R, the success rate increases from 53.2% zero-shot to 73.6% one-shot, exceeding the solid baseline π0.5 (46.0%). Similar gains are observed on RoboDojo, where success rate improves from 35.67% zero-shot to 47.17% one-shot. The same framework also transfers to real-world robots, performing block-in-basket and block stacking on Franka.

ru.title: Мосты между миром цифры и реальностью: VLM для управления роботами
ru.desc: В работе исследуется возможность переноса знаний визуально-языковых моделей (VLM) из цифрового мира в физический для управления роботами. Авторы предлагают RoboDawn — интуитивный интерфейс, позволяющий VLM управлять роботом в замкнутом цикле через дискретные команды перемещения, поворота и захвата. Для улучшения производительности применяется обучение в контексте (in-context learning) с использованием нескольких демонстраций, которые помогают модели адаптироваться к конкретной задаче. Экспериментальные результаты показывают, что RoboDawn достигает состояния искусства без специального обучения, улучшая результаты даже одной демонстрацией и успешно переносясь на реальные роботы.

en.title: Bridging Digital and Physical Worlds with RoboDawn
en.desc: This paper explores whether vision-language models (VLMs) can effectively transfer their intelligence from digital environments to physical robotic control. The authors introduce RoboDawn, an interface that allows VLMs to control robots using simple commands for actions like translation and rotation. Through a closed-loop system, the VLM observes the robot's visual state, decides on actions, and adjusts based on outcomes, demonstrating adaptability. The study shows that RoboDawn achieves high performance in robotic tasks without needing specific training, outperforming existing methods in both simulated and real-world scenarios.

zh.title: 让机器人智能跨越数字与物理的鸿沟
zh.desc: 本文探讨了视觉-语言模型（VLM）在机器人控制中如何从数字世界推广到物理世界。我们提出了RoboDawn，一个人性化的接口，使VLM能够通过简单的命令控制机器人。通过观察当前视觉状态、推理下一步动作并执行，VLM能够在闭环中进行决策。实验结果表明，RoboDawn在没有特定任务训练的情况下，依然能在多个基准测试中取得优异表现，展示了其在零样本和一样本学习中的强大能力。

papers.title: OmniEdu: Open Foundation Models for Learning and Teaching
papers.abstract: Abstract  Educational foundation models must solve problems, understand curriculum structure, diagnose learner difficulties, and provide appropriate instructional support. Existing educational language models often focus on either problem solving or tutoring, with training mixtures organized by source or task rather than capability. We present OmniEdu, an open family of foundation models for K-12 learning and teaching. Its instruction-tuning corpus combines over 100 educational resources and general instruction sources, organized around four capabilities: subject competence, curriculum grounding, diagnostic reasoning, and pedagogical action and scaffolding. Our pipeline integrates deterministic cleaning, semantic auditing and rewriting, task-specific quality scoring, token-budgeted diversity selection, and pedagogical instruction assignment. It yields 69,999 examples and 15.96M supervised response tokens, including 60,951 education-specific examples. We fine-tune 4B, 9B, and 27B models and evaluate curriculum grounding, K-12 problem solving, and pedagogical tutoring, alongside general capability. Education-oriented tuning consistently improves all three educational benchmark groups across model scales. OmniEdu-27B achieves 63.12% EM and 76.69% F1 on K12-Bench, 85.89% on MathFish, 86.95% on EDUMATH, and 78.74% in MathTutorBench's Scaffold setting. It also achieves the highest Teaching average on LongTutor among the evaluated models, at 3.02. These results demonstrate the value of curated, capability-balanced supervision for adapting general language models to educational tasks spanning problem solving, curriculum understanding, and instructional support.
affiliations: University of the Chinese Academy of Sciences

ru.title: Универсальная образовательная модель для решения задач и персонализированного обучения
ru.desc: OmniEdu — это семейство открытых foundation models, специально адаптированных для образования K-12. Модели обучены на corpus из более 100 образовательных ресурсов, организованном вокруг четырёх ключевых навыков: предметная компетентность, понимание учебной программы, диагностика трудностей обучающихся и педагогическая поддержка. Авторы разработали комплексный pipeline обработки данных, включающий очистку, семантический аудит, оценку качества и сбалансированное разнообразие примеров, в результате чего получили 69,999 примеров обучения. Модели размерами 4B, 9B и 27B показывают значительное улучшение на образовательных бенчмарках, демонстрируя ценность целенаправленной настройки больших языковых моделей для задач обучения и преподавания.

en.title: Empowering K-12 Education with OmniEdu Models
en.desc: The paper introduces OmniEdu, a set of foundation models designed specifically for K-12 education. These models are trained using a diverse instruction-tuning corpus that includes over 100 educational resources, focusing on four key capabilities: subject competence, curriculum grounding, diagnostic reasoning, and pedagogical support. The authors detail a comprehensive pipeline for data preparation, which includes cleaning, auditing, and quality scoring to ensure high-quality training examples. Results show that OmniEdu models significantly outperform existing educational benchmarks, demonstrating the effectiveness of tailored instruction for enhancing learning and teaching processes.

zh.title: OmniEdu：教育领域的智能基础模型
zh.desc: 本论文介绍了OmniEdu，一个针对K-12教育的基础模型系列。它通过结合超过100个教育资源和一般指导来源，专注于四个能力：学科能力、课程基础、诊断推理和教学支持。研究表明，教育导向的微调显著提高了模型在教育基准测试中的表现，包括问题解决和课程理解。OmniEdu-27B模型在多个教育任务中表现优异，展示了为教育任务定制的监督学习的重要性。

papers.title: Document Retrieval-Aware Chunking (D-RAC): Universal Retrieval-Aware Ingestion of Enterprise Documents via PDF Normalization and Multimodal Markdown Conversion
papers.abstract: Abstract  Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems over enterprise knowledge bases must ingest heterogeneous document formats -- PDFs, Word documents, presentations, and scans -- whose content is locked inside complex visual layouts, multi-column pages, and dense tables. Rule-based extraction and OCR destroy reading order, flatten tables, and lose heading hierarchy, while fully agentic chunking over extracted text incurs high token costs and hallucination risk. We present Document Retrieval-Aware Chunking (D-RAC), an extension of our Web Retrieval-Aware Chunking (W-RAC) framework to arbitrary document formats. D-RAC first normalizes any input document into PDF, exploiting the fact that virtually every format has a faithful, deterministic PDF rendering. A single multimodal LLM pass then converts rendered pages into retrieval-optimized Markdown -- rewriting tables as self-contained prose statements and preserving heading hierarchy -- after which chunking proceeds exactly as in W-RAC: deterministic parsing into ID-addressable units followed by lightweight LLM-based chunk planning over identifiers rather than text. Source text is never regenerated during chunking, preserving W-RAC's cost, determinism, and observability benefits while unlocking every renderable format as a first-class input. On the 236-document, 795-page PDF subset of the RAG-Multi-Corpus benchmark spanning five enterprise domains, D-RAC converts and chunks the entire corpus in 72 minutes with zero errors, producing 1,748 retrieval-ready chunks. Compared to agentic chunking with frontier LLMs, D-RAC reduces chunking-stage output tokens by 95.7%, cutting chunking cost by 77.8% (GPT-4.1 pricing) to 85.6% (Gemini 2.5 Pro pricing) and chunking time by 75%. D-RAC scales linearly to documents of 500+ pages.

ru.title: Умная обработка документов для поиска без потери качества
ru.desc: В статье представлен метод Document Retrieval-Aware Chunking (D-RAC) для обработки разнородных форматов документов в системах Retrieval-Augmented Generation. Подход нормализует любой входной документ в PDF формат, а затем использует мультимодальный LLM для преобразования страниц в оптимизированный для поиска Markdown с сохранением структуры таблиц и заголовков. Система применяет детерминированный парсинг и лёгкое планирование на уровне идентификаторов вместо полного текста, что значительно снижает затраты токенов и риск галлюцинаций. Экспериментальные результаты показывают 95.7% сокращение выходных токенов и ускорение обработки в 75 раз по сравнению с агентными подходами.

en.title: Efficient Document Processing for RAG Systems with D-RAC
en.desc: The paper introduces Document Retrieval-Aware Chunking (D-RAC), a method designed to efficiently process various document formats for Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) systems. D-RAC normalizes documents into PDF format, allowing for consistent rendering and easier extraction of content while maintaining the original structure. It utilizes a multimodal large language model (LLM) to convert these PDFs into retrieval-optimized Markdown, ensuring that tables and headings are preserved. This approach significantly reduces token costs and processing time compared to traditional methods, making it scalable for large documents.

zh.title: 文档处理的新突破：D-RAC
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为文档检索感知分块（D-RAC）的新方法，旨在处理企业知识库中的各种文档格式，如PDF和Word文档。D-RAC首先将输入文档标准化为PDF格式，以便更好地提取信息，并将内容转换为检索优化的Markdown格式。该方法通过轻量级的LLM（大语言模型）进行分块，确保在分块过程中不会重新生成源文本，从而保持成本和可预测性。实验结果表明，D-RAC在处理236个文档的同时，能够以极低的错误率和显著降低的成本完成任务。

papers.title: VideoGen-Agent: Reinforcing Video Generation Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Recent advances in video generative models have enabled high-fidelity, temporally coherent video generation. However, these models often struggle to satisfy prompts requiring specialized knowledge, specific identities, physical consistency, or ordered events. In this paper, we present VideoGen-Agent, a multimodal agent trained through multitask agentic reinforcement learning to use external tools for video generation. The agent coordinates augmentation, generation, and verification tools through multi-turn interactions, using the prompt and intermediate observations to guide its decisions. We train a shared policy on a category-balanced dataset spanning six tasks. Supervised fine-tuning on teacher-generated trajectories establishes tool-use behavior, which is then refined through reinforcement learning. A category-aware hybrid reward evaluates tool-call validity, task-appropriate tool use, and generated video quality. We further introduce VABench, a held-out benchmark of 600 prompts covering procedural knowledge, single- and multi-entity identity preservation, physical consistency, scene composition, and multi-shot temporal structure. On VABench, VideoGen-Agent improves over its base text-to-video generator by 19.1 points, from 56.5 to 75.6. Upgrading the generation tools further raises the score to 86.1 without additional agent training. Human raters prefer the upgraded configuration over the strongest standalone baseline in 84.3% of comparisons. These results support learning tool use across video-generation tasks and show that the trained agent can benefit from subsequent advances in generation tools.

ru.title: Агент-координатор инструментов для генерации видео высокого качества
ru.desc: В статье представлен VideoGen-Agent — мультимодальный агент, обученный с использованием многозадачного обучения с подкреплением для работы с внешними инструментами при генерации видео. Агент координирует инструменты расширения, генерации и верификации через многошаговые взаимодействия, используя промпт и промежуточные наблюдения для принятия решений. Обучение проводится через supervised fine-tuning на учительских траекториях с последующим усовершенствованием через reinforcement learning с гибридной наградой, учитывающей корректность использования инструментов и качество видео. На новом бенчмарке VABench агент достигает улучшения на 19.1 пункта, достигая 75.6 из 100, при этом люди предпочли его результаты базовым решениям в 84.3% случаев.

en.title: Empowering Video Generation with Intelligent Tool Use
en.desc: This paper introduces VideoGen-Agent, a multimodal agent designed to enhance video generation by using external tools. It employs multitask agentic reinforcement learning to improve the quality and coherence of generated videos based on specific prompts. The agent learns to coordinate various tools through interactions, refining its approach with a hybrid reward system that evaluates tool effectiveness and video quality. The results demonstrate significant improvements in video generation tasks, showcasing the agent's ability to adapt and leverage advancements in generation tools.

zh.title: 视频生成的新智能体：VideoGen-Agent
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为VideoGen-Agent的多模态智能体，旨在通过多任务强化学习来生成高质量的视频。该智能体能够协调增强、生成和验证工具，通过多轮交互来满足特定的生成需求。我们在一个平衡的数据集上训练了共享策略，并通过监督微调和强化学习来优化工具使用行为。实验结果表明，VideoGen-Agent在处理复杂视频生成任务时，显著提高了生成质量和工具使用的有效性。

papers.title: onPanda: Efficient Annotation of On-Policy Alignment Data for LLMs and Agents via Token-Level Correction
papers.abstract: Abstract  We present onPanda, an interactive tool for efficiently annotating LLM alignment data and agent trajectories. onPanda adopts token-level correction as its core interaction: while reading a model response, the annotator locates the first inappropriate token and either picks a substitute from the model's candidate tokens or types the correct text via free-form editing. The system then truncates everything after that position and continues generation from the corrected prefix, repeating this locate-correct-continue loop until a satisfactory response is obtained. This mechanism lets annotators precisely steer model outputs at low cost: a small controlled study suggests that onPanda reduces median annotation time by 52% over manual post-editing. Since the vast majority of tokens in the final response are generated by the model itself, the resulting data largely preserves the model's sampling distribution and is well suited for constructing on-policy SFT and preference data. Furthermore, the token-level corrections recorded during annotation provide fine-grained supervision with precise positions and naturally paired positive--negative samples. onPanda also connects to external tools and harnesses, enabling interactive trajectory annotation in realistic environments. In addition, we release Panda-CVL, a dataset annotated with onPanda, together with a benchmark for token-level correction.

ru.title: Эффективная аннотация с точной коррекцией на уровне токенов
ru.desc: В статье представлена интерактивная система onPanda для эффективной аннотации данных для выравнивания больших языковых моделей и траекторий агентов. Основной механизм основан на коррекции на уровне токенов: аннотатор находит первый неправильный токен в ответе модели и либо выбирает замену из кандидатов модели, либо вводит правильный текст вручную, после чего система продолжает генерацию с исправленного префикса. Такой подход сокращает медианное время аннотации на 52% по сравнению с ручным редактированием, при этом сохраняя распределение выборки модели, что делает данные пригодными для обучения с контролем учителя и создания данных предпочтений. Авторы также выпускают датасет Panda-CVL и бенчмарк для оценки качества коррекции на уровне токенов.

en.title: Efficient Annotation with onPanda: Correct, Continue, and Conquer!
en.desc: The paper introduces onPanda, a tool designed to help users annotate data for aligning large language models (LLMs) and tracking agent behaviors. It focuses on a token-level correction method, allowing annotators to identify and correct specific tokens in model responses, which can then be regenerated from the corrected point. This iterative process significantly reduces the time needed for annotation, as shown by a study indicating a 52% decrease compared to traditional methods. Additionally, onPanda generates high-quality data suitable for supervised fine-tuning (SFT) and preference learning, while also providing detailed supervision through recorded corrections.

zh.title: onPanda：高效的交互式标注工具
zh.desc: 本文介绍了onPanda，这是一个用于高效标注大语言模型（LLM）对齐数据和代理轨迹的交互工具。onPanda的核心交互方式是基于令牌级别的修正，标注者在阅读模型响应时，首先定位到第一个不合适的令牌，然后可以从模型的候选令牌中选择替代项，或通过自由编辑输入正确文本。该系统会截断该位置之后的所有内容，并从修正后的前缀继续生成，重复这一定位-修正-继续的循环，直到获得满意的响应。通过这种机制，标注者能够以低成本精确引导模型输出，研究表明onPanda的标注时间比手动后期编辑减少了52%。

papers.title: Grounded Action Model: 3D Grounding as a Foundation for Robotics
papers.abstract: Abstract  Manipulation policies must know which objects matter and where they are, yet the pretrained backbones that current robot foundation models build on, from language in vision-language-action models (VLAs) to video generation in world-action models (WAMs), do not directly require this metric grounding, leaving it to be learned implicitly from robot demonstrations. We propose Grounded Action Models (GAMs), a new paradigm of robot foundation models built with 3D grounding. GAM can be conditioned using language, points, or box prompts, which are first transformed into a shared object-centric representation of the selected objects. This representation captures target-focused visual features and metric object geometry, which is mixed with robot state history through a multi-stream transformer to predict action chunks. Although GAMs can be run autonomously, they can also serve as a low-level controller that a high-level planner controls using its various input modalities, allowing for long-horizon and memory-dependent manipulation. On RoboTwin 2.0, GAM achieves an average success rate of 55.3% across 50 tasks (vs. 52.0% for Spatial Forcing), including 47.6% under scene randomization (vs. 30.4% for Abot-M0), with its action policy trained only on clean-scene demonstrations. On LIBERO-PRO, it achieves a state-of-the-art average success rate of 61% (vs. 53% for π_{0.5}) across 16 perturbation settings, with the largest gains when targets are relocated or newly designated. On two real robots, GAM retains 17/20 successes under visual shift on a bimanual YAM versus 4/20 for π_{0.5}, while its composition with a Molmo2 planner on a Franka achieves 64.7% ID and 49.8% OOD step completion on long-horizon and memory-dependent tasks.

ru.title: Робототехника с метрическим пониманием: фундаментальные модели с 3D-разметкой для точной манипуляции
ru.desc: В работе предлагается новая парадигма фундаментальных моделей для робототехники под названием Grounded Action Models (GAM), которые используют 3D-разметку для лучшего понимания объектов манипуляции и их геометрии. Модель может быть кондиционирована с помощью естественного языка, точечных указателей или bounding box'ов, которые преобразуются в единое объектно-центричное представление, содержащее визуальные признаки и метрические характеристики объектов. Трансформер с несколькими потоками объединяет это представление с историей состояния робота для предсказания последовательностей действий, позволяя как автономную работу, так и интеграцию с высокоуровневыми планировщиками. GAM демонстрирует значительное улучшение на бенчмарках RoboTwin 2.0 и LIBERO-PRO, а также показывает лучшую устойчивость к визуальным сдвигам и обобщение на реальных роботах.

en.title: Grounded Action Models: Enhancing Robot Manipulation with 3D Awareness
en.desc: The paper introduces Grounded Action Models (GAMs), a new type of robot foundation model that incorporates 3D grounding to enhance manipulation tasks. Unlike previous models that rely on implicit learning from demonstrations, GAMs utilize a shared object-centric representation that combines visual features and object geometry with robot state history. This allows GAMs to predict action sequences more effectively and can be controlled by high-level planners for complex tasks. The results show that GAMs outperform existing models in various benchmarks, demonstrating their effectiveness in both simulated and real-world environments.

zh.title: 有向动作模型：提升机器人操作能力的新范式
zh.desc: 本文提出了一种新的机器人基础模型——有向动作模型（GAM），它通过3D定位来增强机器人的操作能力。GAM能够使用语言、点或框提示进行条件设置，并将这些信息转化为以对象为中心的共享表示，捕捉目标相关的视觉特征和度量几何。该模型通过多流变换器与机器人状态历史混合，以预测动作片段，支持自主运行和高层规划控制。实验结果表明，GAM在多个任务中表现优异，成功率显著高于现有模型，尤其在目标重新定位时表现最佳。

papers.title: One to More, More to One: Category-Aware Iterative Expert Training for Software Engineering Agents
papers.abstract: Abstract  Repository-level software engineering (SWE) comprises heterogeneous task categories, whose progress under pooled agentic reinforcement learning can be uneven: gains in some categories coincide with regressions in others, while aggregate resolution obscures these changes. Motivated by this category see-saw, we develop a category-aware expert-training and policy-integration framework. Executable task construction and SWE Labeler, an evidence-grounded multi-axis labeling system, organize the training pools. Initial category-specific RL improves average training success while leaving uneven instance-level progress, motivating explicit consolidation of successful behavior and policy-adaptive task selection. Same-origin category experts alternate long-horizon Agentic-miniRL with Refresh-Repair-Expand (RRE): the updated policy refreshes instance mastery, reuses its own verified successful trajectories for Repair SFT, and reselects tasks for further RL. Label-routed multi-teacher on-policy distillation (MOPD) consolidates the experts into one deployable student, with ReLU-gated reward extrapolation keeping only each teacher's improving direction over the reference. Expert training and policy integration require no external model to provide solution trajectories or action targets. We evaluate Pooled RL and Balanced RL, expert development, and single-model integration through aggregate and per-category resolution, the minimum category lift over each joint-RL baseline, and expert-gain recovery. The final MOPD policy achieves mean resolution of 58.04% on Pro-618 and 59.00% on SWE-bench Multilingual, improving over the base model by 5.39 and 2.78 percentage points, respectively.

ru.title: Сбалансированное обучение агентов через категорийных экспертов и интеграцию политик
ru.desc: В этой работе предлагается фреймворк для обучения агентов в задачах инженерии ПО на уровне репозитория, где различные категории задач требуют сбалансированного прогресса. Авторы используют категорий-специфичных экспертов, которые обучаются с помощью reinforcement learning и процедуры Refresh-Repair-Expand для консолидации успешного поведения. Интеграция экспертов осуществляется через многоучительское дистиллирование политики (MOPD) с использованием gated-механизма для сохранения улучшающих направлений каждого учителя. Предложенный подход достигает значительного улучшения в разрешении задач без необходимости внешних моделей для предоставления решений.

en.title: Enhancing Task Performance in Software Engineering with Category-Aware Reinforcement Learning
en.desc: This paper addresses the challenges in repository-level software engineering (SWE) where different task categories can progress unevenly under pooled agentic reinforcement learning (RL). The authors propose a category-aware framework that includes expert training and policy integration to improve task performance. They introduce a multi-axis labeling system and a method for consolidating successful behaviors while adapting task selection based on category-specific performance. The results show that their approach leads to significant improvements in task resolution metrics compared to baseline models, demonstrating the effectiveness of their method in managing heterogeneous task categories.

zh.title: 优化软件工程任务的强化学习策略
zh.desc: 本论文探讨了在软件工程中，如何通过强化学习处理不同任务类别的进展不均衡问题。我们提出了一种类别感知的专家训练和策略整合框架，以提高训练效果。通过构建可执行任务和多轴标签系统，优化了训练池的组织。最终的多教师在线蒸馏策略显著提高了模型在多个基准上的表现，展示了专家训练和策略整合的有效性。

papers.title: Deep Persona: A Psychologically Grounded Architecture and Evaluation Framework for Role-Playing Agents and Simulations
papers.abstract: Abstract  Existing approaches to persona simulation with Large Language Models (LLMs) mostly rely on shallow character descriptions that fail to sustain coherent character behavior across extended interactions. We introduce Deep Persona, a psychologically grounded, three-layered architecture that organizes personas into hierarchical levels of observable expression, latent beliefs, and core motivational drives, for constructing highly convincing role-playing agents. Governed by the principles of scripted determinism and bounded agency, the architecture restricts the model to a reactive engine guided by a structured internal script. We further propose a reference-free evaluation framework that benchmarks dialogue naturalness against empirical human distributions using established psychological clinical instruments and adversarial stress-tests. Empirical evaluation reveals that while LLMs achieve high pragmatic fluency, they exhibit systematic limitations in emotional expression and joint attention. In addition, we present a case study of two Deep Personas and evaluate them using the proposed framework, demonstrating that structured personas can produce interactions that more closely align with human conversational behavior.

ru.title: Психологическая глубина вместо поверхностных описаний: структурированные персоны для реалистичного диалога
ru.desc: Статья предлагает Deep Persona — трёхуровневую архитектуру для создания убедительных персонажей в диалоговых системах на основе больших языковых моделей. Архитектура организует персоны иерархически: наблюдаемые действия, скрытые убеждения и глубокие мотивационные установки, что обеспечивает последовательное поведение персонажа на протяжении длительного взаимодействия. Авторы разработали новую методику оценки качества диалогов без эталонных ответов, используя психологические инструменты и стресс-тесты. Исследование показало, что структурированные персоны с психологическим обоснованием воспроизводят человеческое поведение в разговорах более естественно, чем стандартные подходы LLM.

en.title: Deep Persona: Enhancing Character Realism in AI Conversations
en.desc: This paper presents Deep Persona, a new architecture for simulating characters in conversations using Large Language Models (LLMs). Unlike previous methods that use simple character traits, Deep Persona organizes personas into three layers: observable behaviors, hidden beliefs, and core motivations. This structured approach allows for more realistic and coherent interactions by guiding the model's responses with a defined internal script. The authors also introduce a new evaluation method to measure how natural the dialogue is compared to real human conversations, revealing that while LLMs are fluent, they struggle with emotional depth and attention in interactions.

zh.title: 深度角色：提升对话自然性的心理学架构
zh.desc: 本文介绍了一种名为Deep Persona的架构，用于提升大型语言模型（LLMs）在角色扮演中的表现。该架构通过三层次的心理学基础组织角色，包括可观察的表现、潜在信念和核心动机驱动，从而构建出更具说服力的角色代理。我们还提出了一种无参考的评估框架，通过心理学临床工具和对抗性压力测试来评估对话的自然性。实证评估表明，尽管LLMs在实用流畅性上表现良好，但在情感表达和共同注意力方面存在系统性局限。

papers.title: Harness-Zero: Harness Distillation via Agent-as-Harness
papers.abstract: Abstract  Agent harnesses, the external systems that mediate model-environment interaction, can substantially improve agent performance, but their gains remain tied to the harness at deployment. Because the best harness varies across domains, instances, and models, a general-purpose agent must either settle for a suboptimal shared harness or route among an ever-growing set of specialized ones. We therefore study agent harness distillation: using a domain- or instance-optimized harness as training-time guidance and transferring the behaviors it induces into model weights, so that its gains survive under a single fixed target harness. The challenge is that the two harnesses differ in action space and available information, so guidance from the optimized harness cannot serve directly as supervision for the target one. We introduce Harness-Zero, which enables harness distillation through agent-as-harness. Guided by the optimized harness, a harnessing agent corrects student responses before execution in the target harness's action space, turning harness guidance into training demonstrations. Fine-tuning on the resulting trajectories internalizes harness-induced behavior into the model, so the specialized harness can be removed at deployment. Our experiments spanning knowledge work, tool use, and science domains show that: (1) For frontier LLMs using the same evolved harness, agent-as-harness outperforms code-as-harness. (2) With the specialized harness removed at deployment, Harness-Zero improves the base model's macro-average task success from 23.3% to 44.3%, even exceeding the 41.7% it reaches with that harness still attached. (3) Harness-Zero recovers harness-induced behaviors absent from the base model, with 82.3% average recovery across 28 patterns in the three domains.
